translationRepairs: His daughter Boertai became Genghis Khans Radiant Offering Assisting Sagely Empress.
His daughter Boertai became Genghis Khan's Radiant Offering Assisting Sagely Empress.

The Chinese identifies Boertai as Taizu's empress (太祖光獻翼聖皇后). English 'Genghis Khans' lacks the possessive apostrophe and can be read as fusing the khan's name into the title; the proposed 'Genghis Khan's' is grammatical and faithful.
His son Anchannayan followed Genghis Khan on thirty-two campaigns, helping pacify Western Xia, sever the Tong Pass route, and capture the Uyghur city of Xingsigan.
His son Anchen followed Genghis Khan on thirty-two campaigns, helping pacify Western Xia, sever the Tong Pass route, and capture the Uyghur city of Xingsigan.
This sentence names the son 按陳 only. 按陳那顏 is the later granted style in the next unit (歲丁亥，賜號國舅按陳那顏), so rendering him Anchannayan here is unsupported.

When Ariq Böke rebelled, in 1261 he joined the princes on the northern campaign with ten sons including Hahai, Tuohuan, and Woluochen. At Manglai he fought Ariq Bökes partisan Baerhabaersi from Shimur, pursued north to Boluoketu, and fought again from dawn to dusk, taking ten thousand heads until corpses covered the plain.

When Ariq Böke rebelled, in 1261 he joined the princes on the northern campaign with ten sons including Hahai, Tuohuan, and Woluochen. At Manglai he fought Ariq Böke's partisan Baerhabaersi from Shimur, pursued north to Boluoketu, and fought again from dawn to dusk, taking ten thousand heads until corpses covered the plain.
阿里不哥之黨 is 'Ariq Böke's partisans'. The missing apostrophe in 'Ariq Bökes' is a real grammatical error; the replacement does not change meaning.
In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he joined the emperors personal campaign, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jining Commandery for his merit, and granted a white parasol canopy.
In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he joined the emperor's personal campaign, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jining Commandery for his merit, and granted a white parasol canopy.
從帝親征 is following the emperor on a personal campaign. 'Emperors personal' lacks the required possessive; 'emperor's personal campaign' is the correct English.

At that time Wuzong, holding a princely command on the northern frontier, was ordered to place Manzitai in overall charge of Mongol military and civilian offices and transfer him to garrison Manglai against the north.

At that time Wuzong was holding a princely command, leading a great army to guard the northern frontier; an edict ordered Manzitai to take overall charge of Mongol military and civilian offices and transfer to Wuzong's garrison at Manglai to check the north.
有旨令蠻子台 marks Manzitai, not Wuzong, as the person ordered. The proposal restores 轉武宗守莽來 but still makes Wuzong the subject of 'was ordered to place Manzitai'.
In the second year of Zhide he was granted fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang.
In the second year of Zhida he was granted fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang.
至大 is the Zhida era; Zhide is a different reign title. The idiomatic dating already uses 1309, matching Zhida 2.
During Huangqing she was further enfeoffed as the emperors elder sister, Grand Princess.
During Huangqing she was further enfeoffed as the emperor's elder sister, Grand Princess.
皇姊 is the emperor's elder sister. 'The emperors elder sister' is ungrammatical; the apostrophe is required and does not alter the source meaning.
In the third year of Zhide Diaobubula died and was buried at Mohuaitu.
In the third year of Zhida Diaobubula died and was buried at Mohuaitu.
至大三年 is the third year of Zhida, not Zhide. The idiomatic 'In 1310' already reflects that year.
In the third year of Zhide, only eight years old, he inherited the myriarchate.
In the third year of Zhida, only eight years old, he inherited the myriarchate.
The same 至大三年 dating governs this inheritance; the literal must read Zhida, not Zhide.
During Zhishun Duoerzhiban was enfeoffed as Princess Suoyong Xianning.
During Zhishun Duoerzhiban was enfeoffed as Princess Suyong Xianning.
肅 is sù, so 肅雍 romanizes as Suyong, not Suoyong. The proposed title matches the characters without changing the enfeoffment.
From childhood, by Kublais order, he was raised in Princess Wokezhens household and became the consort Bozhuer; later he inherited four hundred households of his tribes people.
From childhood, by Kublai's order, he was raised in Princess Wokezhen's household and became the consort Bozhuer; later he inherited four hundred households of his tribe's people.
世皇旨, 斡可珍公主所, and 本部民 require possessives in English (Kublai's, Wokezhen's, tribe's). The repairs are grammatical and do not add meaning.
These all inherited princely rank through service as imperial consorts.
These all inherited princely rank through service as imperial sons-in-law.
駙馬 are imperial sons-in-law. 'Imperial consorts' inverts the marriage and can be read as palace wives; 'imperial sons-in-law' is the accurate literal.

Shunzong's Sagely and Offering Meta-empress Daji—enrolled as Grand Empress Dowager by Wuzong in 1307, accorded extended honorifics under Renzong in 1315 and 1320, and eventually styled Grand Empress Dowager—was the daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Hundutiemuer.

Shunzong's Sagely and Offering Primordial Sacred Empress Daji—enrolled as Empress Dowager by Wuzong in 1307, given added honorifics as Empress Dowager in 1310 and again under Renzong in 1315, and in 1320 raised to Grand Empress Dowager—was the daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Hundutiemuer.
元聖 is not 'Meta-empress'. Wuzong's 冊上皇太后 in 大德十一年 is Empress Dowager; 太皇太后 appears only at 延祐七年. The replacement also restores the omitted 至大三年 honorific stage.
When Boluotiemuer died, Maizhuhans grandson Ash inherited the chiliarchate.
When Boluotiemuer died, Maizhuhan's grandson Ash inherited the chiliarchate.
買住罕孫 is Maizhuhan's grandson. 'Maizhuhans' lacks the possessive apostrophe and fuses the name; the proposed form is correct.

Among the women who became empresses—beginning with the Radiant and Assisting Sagely Queen—Xianzong's Chaste and Constant Empress Hudutai and her sister Yesu'er were daughters of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Manggechen.

Among the women who became empresses—beginning with the Radiant and Assisting Sagely Empress—Xianzong's Chaste and Constant Empress Hudutai and her sister Yesu'er were daughters of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Manggechen.
光獻翼聖皇后 is an empress, the same 皇后 rank used for the later women in the sentence. 'Queen' understates Yuan imperial rank.
Wenzong's Empress Budashili was daughter of the King of Diaoa'abulu.
Wenzong's Empress Budashili was daughter of Diaoa'bula, King of Lu.
雕阿不剌魯王 is the man 雕阿不剌 with the title 魯王, not a place-name 'Diaoa'abulu'. The proposed split matches the Chinese.
Wuzong's Kind, Merciful, and Sagely Empress Zhenge was Tuolian's son Bingbula's daughter;
Wuzong's Kind, Merciful, and Sagely Empress Zhenge was Tuolian's son Bengbula's daughter;
迸不剌 is Bèngbùlà. 'Bingbula' invents a second English name for the same man already identified as Bengbula.

He also instructed Anchannayan's son Suoluhuodu: 'Because you and your father have served the state faithfully, you shall dwell east of Komuer Undur, from the Luoma River to Chishan, south along the Tu River, among the imperial people.'

He also instructed Anchannayan's son Suoluhuodu: 'Because you and your father have served the state faithfully, you shall dwell east of Komuer Undur, from the Luoma River to Chishan, south along the Tu River, neighboring the imperial subjects.'
與國民為鄰, like the neighboring clauses in the surrounding grants, means to take the imperial subjects as neighbors, not to dwell among them.

In 1270 the chiliarch Woluochen and his consort Princess Nangjiazhen petitioned the court: 'Our granted territory at Da'er Lake, three hundred li northeast of Shangdu, is our fief's summer encampment; we ask permission to build a walled town there.'

In 1270 the myriarch Woluochen and his consort Princess Nangjiazhen petitioned the court: 'Our granted territory at Da'er Lake, three hundred li northeast of Shangdu, is our fief's summer encampment; we ask permission to build a walled town there.'
斡羅陳萬戶 is a myriarch (commander of ten thousand). Chiliarch renders 千戶, a different office.

By the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the chiliarch Woluochen and his consort Princess Nangjiazhen petitioned the court: 'The nongtu our fief received, at Da'erhaizi three hundred li northeast of Shangdu, is in fact where our fief summers; a walled town may be built to dwell there.'

By the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the myriarch Woluochen and his consort Princess Nangjiazhen petitioned the court: 'The nongtu our fief received, at Da'erhaizi three hundred li northeast of Shangdu, is in fact where our fief summers; a walled town may be built to dwell there.'
The same 萬戶 must be myriarch in the literal field; chiliarch is the wrong office term.
Twenty-two years later it was elevated to Yingchang Circuit.
In the twenty-second year it was changed to Yingchang Circuit.
二十二年 continues the Zhiyuan reign of the preceding 至元七年, i.e. Zhiyuan 22 (1285), not twenty-two years after 1270. 改為 is 'changed to', not a later elevation after a counted interval.
Again Yongping Circuit had Luanzhou and the six counties Lulong, Qianan, Funing, Changli, Shicheng, and Leting; this was granted in the first year of Zhide.
Again Yongping Circuit had Luanzhou and the six counties Lulong, Qianan, Funing, Changli, Shicheng, and Leting; this was granted in the first year of Zhida.
至大元年 is Zhida 1. Zhide is another era name and would misdate the grant.
As for fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang, that was granted in the second year of Zhide.
As for fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang, that was granted in the second year of Zhida.
至大二年 is Zhida 2, matching the idiomatic 1309 grant of the Pingjiang paddies.
Beitu, also of the Yiqiliesi clan, excelled at mounted archery.
Beitu, of the Yiqiliesi clan, excelled at mounted archery.
亦乞列思氏 is the clan name; 亦 is not the adverb 'also'. The idiomatic already omits that false 'also'.
Shi'erchedan reported everything to the emperor; the emperor was greatly pleased and promised him marriage to the imperial younger sister Tiemulun.
Shi'erchedan reported everything to the emperor; the emperor was greatly pleased and promised Beitu marriage to the imperial younger sister Tiemulun.
許妻以皇妹 is the emperor promising Beitu the marriage. After 術兒徹丹具以白帝, literal 'promised him' can be read as promising the envoy; naming Beitu removes the false attribution.
After his imperial sister-in-law died, the emperor gave him his daughter Huochenbieji in marriage and appointed Haribatai's son Yehuohulin to attend him bearing bow and arrows.
After the imperial younger sister died, the emperor gave him his daughter Huochenbieji in marriage and appointed Haribatai's son Yehuohulin to attend him bearing bow and arrows.
皇妹薨 continues 皇妹帖木倫, Genghis Khan's younger sister and Beitu's wife, not a sister-in-law. The proposed 'imperial younger sister' matches the kinship term.

When he died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Sincere in Supporting the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Consort Commandant, Chief Pillar of State; inherited enfeoffment as King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Tranquil.

When he died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Sincere in Supporting the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Holder of the Office Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State; inherited enfeoffment as King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Tranquil.
The Chinese list includes 開府儀同三司 between Grand Preceptor and Consort Commandant. The literal omitted that honor; the replacement restores it.

When Hulian died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Effecting Loyalty in Preserving Virtue in Supporting Transport and Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Consort Commandant, Chief Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Proclaiming.

When Hulian died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Effecting Loyalty in Preserving Virtue in Supporting Transport and Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Proclaiming.
忽憐's posthumous grants likewise include 開府儀同三司, present in the Chinese and the idiomatic but dropped from the literal.
The Jin source lineage used mountains as ramparts to limit north and south; Alawusitijihuli with one army guarded its strategic point.
The Jin used mountains as ramparts to divide north from south; Alawusitijihuli with one army guarded the strategic point.
金源氏 is a designation of the Jin dynasty, not a 'source lineage'. The calque obscures the polity that built the mountain barrier.

After Genghis Khan secured Yunzhong he found them through a reward offer and treated them generously. He posthumously enfeoffed Alawusitijihuli as King of Gaotang and Alihei as Princess of Gaotang. Because Xueyaohe was still young, he first enfeoffed the nephew Zhenguo as King of Beiping.

After Genghis Khan secured Yunzhong he found them through a reward offer and treated them generously. He posthumously enfeoffed Alawusitijihuli as King of Gaotang and Alihei as Consort of the King of Gaotang. Because Xueyaohe was still young, he first enfeoffed the nephew Zhenguo as King of Beiping.
高唐王妃 is consort of the King of Gaotang, parallel to 高唐王. 公主 would be princess; calling Alihei Princess of Gaotang conflates ranks.
In Renzongs reign he was again granted the tax revenue of Ningchang County.
In Renzong's reign he was again granted the tax revenue of Ningchang County.
仁宗朝 is Renzong's reign. The missing apostrophe makes the English ungrammatical without changing the date or grant.
Ash married Temürs daughter Princess Yilihaya and later Möngkes great-granddaughter Princess Maide.
Ash married Temür's daughter Princess Yilihaya and later Möngke's great-granddaughter Princess Maide.
成宗女 and 憲宗曾孫女 require English possessives. 'Temürs' and 'Möngkes' are ungrammatical; the proposed forms match the kinship.
Hulians cousin Buhua married Kublais daughter Princess Wuluzhen;
Hulian's cousin Buhua married Kublai's daughter Princess Wuluzhen;
忽憐從弟 and 世祖女 need possessives in English. The apostrophes restore grammar without altering 從弟 or the marriage.
his younger brother Suolangha married Prince Mangge'as daughter Princess Nuwulun; their daughter became Wuzongs Benevolent Offering Sagely Empress and bore Mingzong.
his younger brother Suolangha married Prince Mangge'a's daughter Princess Nuwulun; their daughter became Wuzong's Benevolent Offering Sagely Empress and bore Mingzong.
皇子忙哥剌女 and 武宗仁獻章聖皇后 require possessives. The proposal only supplies the missing apostrophes.

The princess was bright and wise in counsel; when the imperial carriage campaigned in all directions she was often left to hold the capital; on great affairs of army and state he consulted and reported before acting; on campaign he had no worry of affairs at home—the princesss power was greatest in this.

The princess was bright and wise in counsel; when the imperial carriage campaigned in all directions she was often left to hold the capital; on great affairs of army and state he consulted and reported before acting; on campaign he had no worry of affairs at home—the princess's power was greatest in this.
公主之力 is the princess's effort. Literal 'princesss' is a misspelled possessive; 'princess's' is the grammatical form.
Princess Alahaibieji was posthumously made Grand Princess of Qi and further enfeoffed as Princess of Zhao.
Princess Alahaibieji was posthumously made Imperial Grand-Aunt and Grand Princess of Qi, and further enfeoffed in the Zhao princedom.

The source has 皇祖姑齊國大長公主 and 加封趙國. The original omits the grand-aunt rank and treats 趙國 as 'Princess of Zhao'. The proposal restores both facts but the stacked 'imperial grand-aunt Grand Princess' is awkward.

The emperor once sent his retainer Axisi as envoy to the enemy camp. Spotted in the crowd, Kuolijisi immediately asked after the emperors' health and then after his heir. Before he could finish speaking, attendants pulled Axisi away.

The emperor once sent his household retainer Axisi as special envoy to the enemy territory. Spotted in the crowd, Kuolijisi immediately asked whether the two palaces were well and then how his heir was. Before he could finish speaking, attendants pulled Axisi away.
兩宮 is the two palaces, not a plural 'emperors'. 家臣 and 特使敵境 are household retainer and special envoy to enemy territory. The original misreads 兩宮 and thins those terms.

Prince of Qiyang Yuechicha'er and Chancellor Tuohuchubadulu dispatched five hundred soldiers to escort the party to the burial site. When the coffin was opened for the funeral rites the body appeared as if alive, and Kuolijisi was brought home for burial.

Prince of Qiyang Yuechicha'er and Chancellor Tuohuchubadulu dispatched five hundred soldiers to escort them to the burial place. After libation and announcement they opened and viewed the coffin—the corpse was as if alive—and thus they were able to return him for burial.
This unit never names 闊裏吉思. It records escort to the burial place, 奠告啟視, the corpse as if alive, and 歸葬. Inserting Kuolijisi and dropping the libation-and-viewing is unsupported.
